intended_object: The space of simple (elementary) predictable processes: the linear span, inside L²(ℝ≥0 × Ω, predictable σ-algebra, Leb ⊗ P), of the processes 1_(a,b](t)·Z(ω) with a ≤ b and Z an 𝓕_a-measurable L² random variable. Inferred from the docstring, the name, and its use in the density argument in PredictableDensity.lean.
explanation: The body is Submodule.span ℝ of the set of elementaryPredictable 𝓕 a b Z, over all a ≤ b and Z ∈ lpMeas ℝ ℝ (𝓕 a) 2 P. In ClarkOcone.lean, elementaryPredictable is the L² class of the tensor product 1_(a,b] ⊗ Z, seen in PredictableProcessL2 𝓕 P (predictable-measurable classes in L²(Leb ⊗ P)). This is the textbook class of simple predictable integrands. The 1_{0}×F₀ terms are left out, but they have Leb ⊗ P measure zero and are zero in L². The condition a ≤ b is harmless. Coefficients are general 𝓕_a-measurable L² variables, which gives the standard span. Generality: the section's variables include a Gaussian measure on a Banach space, but the definition does not depend on them. The next lemma, elementaryPredictable_mem_span, omits all the normed-space and IsGaussian instances and still uses elementaryPredictableSpan, and the code compiles, so Lean pruned the unused instances. The definition therefore only needs a measurable space with an s-finite measure and a filtration indexed by ℝ≥0. Real values and time ℝ≥0 are the standard setting for this notion. A search of Mathlib for ElementaryPredictable, SimpleProcess and elementaryPredictable found nothing, so there is no counterpart.
